description: A nightly database backup automated into a script that masks pg_dump's failure behind a pipe, ignores the copy's result, deletes the last good backup first, logs 'backup done' regardless, and dropped the restore check.

defects.tell: pg_dump runs on the left of a pipe into gzip with no pipefail and no set -e, so its failure is lost and gzip writes an empty stream; three nights of 'password authentication failed' went unnoticed
the runbook checks the file is at least 50 MB and arrived with the same size; the script checks neither, and the files on the backup server are 20 bytes
scp ... || true discards the copy's exit status, so a backup that never reached the vault is reported the same as one that did
rm -f appointments-*.sql.gz runs first, so an interrupted or failing run leaves no local backup at all; the runbook keeps 14 days and deletes only old ones
the log says 'backup done' after every failure; it names no file, size or destination, so a run that did nothing looks exactly like one that worked
the weekly restore into the scratch database, the only step that proves a backup can be used, was left out of the automation and is not listed as something the script does not do

control.tell: the schedule is right: daily at 02:30, the quiet hour, as the manual backup ran, with output appended to the log. A report that faults the schedule is inventing.
